rec.name: My Account: Product Documentation & Invoice Download
rec.status: Built — marked done (✓ in comments), implementation details undocumented

what.text: The customer's My Account area is extended so a logged-in customer can download (a) product documentation (manuals, data sheets and similar) that depends on the items they ordered, and (b) the invoice for each order. The ticket title also mentions 'uploading' invoices, which most likely means the shop uploads or attaches the invoice file so the customer can fetch it.

why.text: Self-service access to invoices and product documents after purchase reduces post-purchase uncertainty and support requests. It signals professionalism and reliability, which is especially useful for technical or B2B-style products. It also gives customers a reason to log in again, which supports repeat purchases and later re-engagement. This is an inferred rationale, as the ticket does not state one.

how.text: Use classic customer accounts, not the new customer accounts. Maximilian called this 'mandatory'. The DEV team was briefed to show the documentation per ordered article, plus invoices, inside the account order view. The work was tracked as 'Sectionfy | Doku & Rechnungs Download in MyAccount', which suggests it was built with Sectionfy sections or blocks. Likely approach (inferred): store the document files per product, for example as file metafields. In the customer account order template, loop over the order's line items and render download links for each product's documents. Add an invoice download link per order, using a file attached to the order or an app-provided invoice URL. The exact mechanism is not documented.

items: Which documents are linked to which products (mapping per product/variant) — inferred
Document label / file type shown to the customer — inferred
Invoice source and per-order availability — inferred
Show or hide the documents block when an order has no documents — inferred

dependencies.text: Classic Shopify customer accounts are required (not new customer accounts). It needs theme access to the account/order templates. Per-product document storage (likely product metafields or files) and an invoice source (order attachment or invoice app) are probable but not confirmed. The ticket mentions Sectionfy and a DEV team member (Abhishek).

items: Share of logged-in customers who visit the order detail page
Support tickets about invoices or documentation requests
Account login rate and repeat purchase rate
